class.name: FoliageSpawner3D
class.brief_description: Scatters instances of a [Mesh] procedurally inside a configurable box volume.
class.description: [FoliageSpawner3D] fills a box-shaped volume with randomly placed and oriented copies of [member mesh], similar to Unreal Engine's Procedural Foliage Spawner. It is a specialized [MultiMeshInstance3D]: the generated instances are stored and rendered as a [MultiMesh], but that [MultiMesh] is created automatically and should not be edited directly. The volume to fill is defined by [member volume_size], centered on the node's origin. Placement is controlled by [member density] (points per square meter of the volume's footprint) and [member min_distance] (a minimum spacing enforced between instances so they don't overlap). A grayscale [member distribution_mask] can be assigned to bias or forbid placement in specific areas, and [member seed] makes generation reproducible. If [member project_on_mesh] is enabled (the default), each candidate point is projected straight down onto the actual triangle surface of the [MeshInstance3D] referenced by [member ground_mesh_path] (e.g. terrain), and points whose surface is steeper than [member max_slope_degrees] are discarded; otherwise points are distributed freely throughout the volume's height. Placement only looks at that node's [Mesh] geometry, never at a [CollisionShape3D] or other physics collider, since a collider can differ noticeably in shape from the mesh it is meant to represent. Instances can optionally be tilted to align with the surface normal ([member align_to_normal]) and receive random rotation, extra random tilt, and random uniform scale for natural-looking variation. Nothing is generated automatically: call [method regenerate] (or press the [b]Regenerate[/b] button in the Inspector) whenever the volume, mesh, ground mesh, or any distribution setting changes. The resulting [MultiMesh] is then saved with the scene, so no extra runtime cost is paid on load. To scatter several kinds of vegetation in the same area, add multiple [FoliageSpawner3D] nodes, one per [Mesh].

method.name: regenerate
method.description: Discards the current instances and generates a new set according to the node's current settings, using [member seed] to seed the random number generator. This can be called both in the editor and at runtime; it requires the node to be inside the [SceneTree] when [member project_on_mesh] is enabled, since it needs to resolve [member ground_mesh_path] and read the referenced node's [Mesh] geometry.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], instances are tilted so their up axis follows the surface normal found by [member project_on_mesh] (blended in by [member align_to_normal_amount]). Has no effect when [member project_on_mesh] is [code]false[/code].
Blends each instance's up axis between world up ([code]0.0[/code]) and the surface normal ([code]1.0[/code]) when [member align_to_normal] is enabled.

The target number of instances per square meter of the volume's XZ footprint ([member volume_size].x × [member volume_size].z). The actual instance count is also limited by [member max_instances], [member min_distance], [member distribution_mask], and [member project_on_mesh].

An optional grayscale mask sampled across the volume's XZ footprint (black = 0.0, white = 1.0) and used as the probability that a given candidate point is kept. Set [member mask_invert] to flip which areas are favored.

The path to a [MeshInstance3D] whose [Mesh] geometry candidate points are projected onto when [member project_on_mesh] is enabled. Only that node's mesh surface is used; its collision shape (if any) is ignored.
If [code]true[/code], inverts the values sampled from [member distribution_mask] (white areas become forbidden, black areas become favored).

A multiplier on the target instance count used to bound how many candidate points [method regenerate] will try before giving up. Increase this if strict [member min_distance] or [member distribution_mask] settings are preventing [member density] from being reached; decrease it to bound worst-case generation time.
A hard cap on the number of instances that can be generated, regardless of [member density] and the volume's size.
The upper bound of the random uniform scale applied to each instance. See also [member min_scale].
When [member project_on_mesh] is enabled, candidate points whose surface normal is tilted more than this many degrees from world up are discarded.
The [Mesh] to scatter throughout the volume. [FoliageSpawner3D] generates nothing until this is set.
The minimum horizontal distance enforced between any two instances, measured on the volume's XZ footprint. Set to [code]0.0[/code] to disable spacing checks.
The lower bound of the random uniform scale applied to each instance. See also [member max_scale].

If [code]true[/code], each candidate point is placed by casting a ray straight down (in the volume's local space) from the top of [member volume_size] and snapping to the closest triangle hit on the [Mesh] of the [MeshInstance3D] referenced by [member ground_mesh_path], honoring [member max_slope_degrees]. This only looks at mesh geometry; no physics or collision shapes are involved. Points that hit nothing are discarded. If [code]false[/code], points are instead placed at a random height inside the volume without any projection.
If [code]true[/code], each instance receives a random rotation around its up axis.
The maximum random tilt, in degrees, applied on top of [member align_to_normal] for natural-looking variation.
Pressing this button in the Inspector calls [method regenerate]. It is not meant to be read or assigned from code; use [method regenerate] directly instead.
The seed used to initialize the random number generator during [method regenerate]. Using the same seed with the same settings always produces the same result.
The size of the box volume that instances are scattered within, centered on the node's origin.
